You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild
T5: Claiming Terraform authoring
T6: The old cover letter is addressed to his current employer: writer must not reuse its 'Insurance is new to me' framing

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Engineer
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer building production services in Java and Kotlin, with experience in REST API
design, PostgreSQL, Kafka and AWS-hosted services. Delivered measurable improvements in data
correctness and automated testing, and participates in production on-call. Seeking to move into a
mainly Python backend role, building on Python scripting experience.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java 11/17, Kotlin; Python for data-fix scripts and Jenkins helpers; Go (learning).
APIs and frameworks: Spring Boot, REST APIs, OpenAPI 3, Spring Cloud Contract.
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS.
Cloud and containers: AWS EKS and S3, Kubernetes, Docker.
Testing and operations: Testcontainers, contract testing, production incident investigation,
incident write-ups.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | 2022-Present
• Build Java/Kotlin Spring Boot microservices using PostgreSQL, Kafka and Kubernetes.
• Designed a versioned partner quoting REST API using OpenAPI 3; added per-partner rate
limiting and contract tests with Spring Cloud Contract. The API supported 12 broker partners
and approximately 400,000 quote requests per month.
• Implemented a transactional outbox and idempotency keys for Kafka consumers to address
duplicate claim records from at-least-once delivery. Duplicates fell from approximately 40 per week
to zero over the following quarter.
• Built an internal Kotlin/Spring Boot service to render policy PDFs, using AWS S3 and SQS.
Wrote the team’s Kotlin coding guidelines for its first Kotlin service.
• Participate in on-call one week per month; handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and
produced a write-up that received praise.
• Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks, since 2024. Work in an entirely English-speaking
environment.
Software Developer | Viajar Online | 2019-2021
• Worked on booking and payments in a large Java application backed by Oracle. Increased
payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer refactoring.
• Extracted email/SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Spring Boot service
using Java 11, RabbitMQ, Thymeleaf and Docker; gained experience with messaging, retries and
operating separate services.
PERSONAL PROJECT
Gopher Weekend | Go CLI
Developing a command-line tool that compares OpenAPI specifications. Approximately 600 lines,
hosted on GitHub; a learning project, not a production service.
CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional Java SE 11 Developer | 2020

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on your Routing & Tracking team. My
production background is in Java and Kotlin, with PostgreSQL, Kafka and Spring Boot, and I
am looking to move into a mainly Python stack. Your work turning carrier events into reliable
shipment tracking is a close match for the problems I have tackled: keeping event-driven data
correct, designing partner-facing APIs and investigating production incidents.
At Tejo Insurance Tech, I addressed duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka
delivery by implementing a transactional outbox and idempotency keys on consumers.
Duplicate claims fell from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. I also
designed a versioned REST API with OpenAPI 3, per-partner rate limiting and contract tests,
supporting 12 broker partners and approximately 400,000 quote requests per month. These
projects offer relevant experience for your event ingestion services and customer-facing
tracking API.
Reliability has also been a practical responsibility. I participate in on-call one week per month
and handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024, producing a write-up that received
praise. Previously, at Viajar Online, I increased payments-module test coverage from 35% to
70% using Testcontainers so we could refactor safely. I work in an entirely English-speaking
environment, wrote our Kotlin coding guidelines and run our fortnightly backend guild
meeting.
My Python experience is currently limited to data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers, rather
than production services. I would bring established backend engineering experience to the
language transition, alongside hands-on work with AWS EKS, S3, SQS and Kubernetes.
Tessel’s emphasis on engineers running their own services and making time for reliability work
aligns with this experience. I would welcome a conversation about how my API and
event-processing work could support your tracking platform.
Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
